archetype (how it wins): My units hurt themselves to grow, then win the front row by striking every round.
removal: overkill: a big strike kills and the damage left over hits the next enemy in reach
holding: every strike leaves the striker bigger, so the unit facing an arrival is too big to kill
the play that feels good (Place): Place: deal 1 to me, I gain +2 strength, then I strike the enemy facing me
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never restores defence or shields its units

archetype (how it wins): A few champions duel the enemy's best units one by one, striking first.
removal: duel: my champion strikes a chosen enemy in its reach first, so it takes no strike back
holding: shields on the champion; it strikes first at any arrival facing it
the play that feels good (Place): Place: I strike the chosen enemy in my reach, first
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never makes tokens or hits many enemies at once

archetype (how it wins): Small damage from many units marks enemies and finishes them anywhere in the lane.
removal: mark and ping: a Marked enemy takes double from strikes; pings finish Bloodied enemies in any row
holding: every enemy placed facing my units is pinged and Marked before it acts
the play that feels good (Place): Place: mark the enemy facing me and deal 1 to it
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never brings cards or units back

archetype (how it wins): My units shove enemies out of the front row and punish them for coming back.
removal: push: the enemy leaves the front row, so it no longer cancels my dot
holding: ambush: an enemy placed facing my unit is hit at once
the play that feels good (Place): Place: push the enemy facing me one row back

archetype (how it wins): Enemies facing my wall can't attack, and enemies that can't attack are killed.
removal: lock: the enemy facing my unit can't attack; my strikes kill an enemy that can't attack outright (Claude's)
holding: locked enemies can't attack the wall that holds the dots
the play that feels good (Place): Place: the enemy facing me can't attack while I face it

archetype (how it wins): I take the enemy's strength away for good until its units are harmless or dead.
removal: weaken: lasting -strength down to 0, then my cards kill units with 0 strength (faeria: Emperor Kaios)
holding: weakened enemies can't hurt my big units with grown defence
the play that feels good (Place): Place: the enemy facing me gets -2 strength for good

archetype (how it wins): Back-row guns hit whole rows when the round starts, before the enemy can move away.
removal: delayed blast: damage set now lands on a whole row at the next round start
holding: every enemy that arrives in the row is hit at the next round start
the play that feels good (Place): Place (back row): at the next round start, deal 2 to every enemy in the enemy front row of this lane
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never shields or restores its units

archetype (how it wins): Back-row units make every damage spell bigger, and spells clear the lane.
removal: burn: damage spells, grown by back-row units, into any row
holding: a damage spell for each arrival; its units stand safe in the back rows
the play that feels good (Place): Place: your next damage spell this round deals +2
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never gives its units more defence

archetype (how it wins): Each spell makes the next one cheaper, and my units react to every spell.
removal: chain: a damage spell deals it again if you cast another spell this round
holding: cheap spells every turn answer every arrival
the play that feels good (Place): Place: your next spell this round costs 1 less; draw 1 if you cast 2 spells this round

archetype (how it wins): I take the enemy's units and copies of his cards, and win with his army.
removal: sides: the enemy unit holding the base becomes mine and holds my dot
holding: the strongest arrival is taken or copied
the play that feels good (Place): Place: copy the enemy facing me into your hand
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never kills its own units for gain

archetype (how it wins): I pick the exact card I need from my deck and play my best cards again and again.
removal: recycle: an enemy unit is shuffled into its owner's deck (Claude's: the library recycles only own cards)
holding: the answer each round is picked from the deck
the play that feels good (Place): Place: pick a card from your deck

archetype (how it wins): I make more supply than anyone, bank it in carry-over and land costly cards early.
removal: banking: a spell paid with all carry-over deals damage equal to what was spent (Claude's; library: cost X in sts1, monster_train)
holding: a full carry-over answers in any lane
the play that feels good (Place): Place: +2 carry-over
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never gains from units standing together

archetype (how it wins): I keep my hand full; cards I discard act, and new cards keep coming.
removal: discard: discard a card to deal its cost as damage to the enemy nearest the base in the lane (Claude's way of on_discard)
holding: a full hand: an answer for each arrival
the play that feels good (Place): Place: discard 1, draw 2

archetype (how it wins): Many cheap units fill every cell, and my cards count them.
removal: count: deal 1 for each ally in my lane to the enemy facing me
holding: all 9 cells filled; a fallen unit's cell is filled again
the play that feels good (Place): Place: put two 1-cell units in free cells beside me
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never has a unit of cost 6+

archetype (how it wins): My units die on purpose, and every death hits the enemy.
removal: offer: my unit dies and its Death effect kills the enemy facing it
holding: every unit that dies hits back
the play that feels good (Place): Place: the ally behind me dies; deal its defence to the enemy facing me

archetype (how it wins): My units die and come back, and each death makes the others deadlier.
removal: mourn: kill an enemy outright if an ally died this round (runeterra: death_count cards)
holding: the dead come back into their cells
the play that feels good (Place): Place: bring back the last ally that died in this lane
blind spot (the one tool it never gets): never deals fixed damage from units' text

archetype (how it wins): My units go back to hand and move, so their Place effects fire again and again.
removal: bounce: the enemy unit goes back to its owner's hand (runeterra Ionia: bounce_enemy)
holding: march: a unit that moved this round can't be attacked (Claude's; library: evasion)
the play that feels good (Place): Place: return an ally to hand; it costs 1 less

archetype (how it wins): Units in full rows, side by side, make each other strong.
removal: rows: every unit of a full row strikes the enemy facing it at once (Claude's)
holding: full rows give every unit in them defence
the play that feels good (Place): Place: if my row is now full, every unit in it gets +1|+1

archetype (how it wins): One big guarded unit holds the lane while the rest shelter behind it.
removal: guard: the guard takes the attack and strikes the attacker back (counterattack)
holding: the guard takes every hit; shields block the first
the play that feels good (Place): Place: join an ally; we become one unit with both stats

archetype (how it wins): My units outlast every fight: hits make them stronger and they are mended each round.
removal: lifesteal: its strikes restore its own defence, so it wins fights over two rounds
holding: round-end mending; each hit survived gives defence
the play that feels good (Place): Place: restore 2 defence to every ally in my row
